candidates.decision_relevance: Would help distinguish persistent participation changes from rebound or deterioration inferred from non-comparable proxy snapshots, and test whether breadth changes precede or follow price moves.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily director outputs repeatedly report Top-100 breadth snapshots with changing membership hashes and differing rolling windows; canonical broad-alt and large-cap breadth are described as unconfirmed.
candidates.metric_name: Point-in-time constituent breadth with stable universe and methodology
candidates.missing_history_problem: No comparable constituent-level historical series is supplied, so changes between snapshots cannot establish participation persistence or sequence.

candidates.decision_relevance: Would clarify whether cited divergent or negative settled flows persisted, reversed, or coincided with price and breadth changes across completed sessions.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily outputs commonly cite a single latest settled ETF session and explicitly state that it does not establish multi-session flow persistence; weekly reviews also cite settled totals without a supplied within-period sequence.
candidates.metric_name: Daily settled BTC and ETH ETF net flows
candidates.missing_history_problem: A multi-session historical sequence aligned to settlement dates is absent from the supplied analyses, limiting assessment of flow persistence and timing relative to market moves.
